paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The graph illustrates the relationship between the rank and the error (RTE), showing how the error changes as the rank varies. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" and has a linear scale, ranging from 4 to 256, with specific values marked at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is labeled "Error (RTE)" and also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.3 to 0.9, with marks at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single line is plotted on the graph, colored black, with green circular markers indicating data points and vertical error bars representing the range of values. The line starts at a value slightly below 0.6 on the y-axis when the rank is 4, decreases to its lowest point at a rank of 16, remains relatively stable at a rank of 64, and then increases to approximately 0.65 when the rank reaches 256.
model_annotations.English: This plot illustrates the relationship between rank and error measured in RTE. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" with a logarithmic scale, ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is labeled "Error (RTE)" with a linear scale, spanning from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick labels at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single line is shown, colored black with green circle markers and solid line style, representing the change in error across different ranks; it starts at approximately 0.53 at a rank of 4, decreases to around 0.45 at a rank of 16, remains relatively stable at about 0.46 at a rank of 64, and then increases to roughly 0.66 at a rank of 256, exhibiting a U-shaped trend with the lowest error at a rank of 16. Vertical error bars are present at each data point, indicating the uncertainty or variability in the error measurements.
model_annotations.German: The diagram represents the relationship between the rank of adapters and the error measured in RTE (Recognizing Textual Entailment). The x-axis, labeled "Rank", is on a linear scale, ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at intervals of powers of 4 (4, 16, 64, and 256). The y-axis, labeled "Error (RTE)", is also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick labels at intervals of 0.3. The diagram contains a single black line with green circular markers, representing the error values at different ranks. The line starts at approximately 0.55 error at rank 4, decreases to around 0.45 error at rank 16, remains relatively stable until rank 64 with an error of about 0.46, and then increases to approximately 0.65 error at rank 256. Error bars are present for each data point, indicating the range of uncertainty associated with each measurement.
